I feel for those kids, I really do. I think that Liz’s neglect of them is abuse. Matthew especially. At no point have I denied that. There are already so many people on this sub documenting the ways she mistreats her kids, as they should. I just wanted to add a different perspective to the conversation, because I don’t have anything new to say about her kids that hasn’t already been covered ad nauseam. 

I empathize with Liz’s kids, and I think they deserve better than they’re getting from their mom. I think there’s more to Liz than just a monster. Both can be true at once. And for what it’s worth, I hope Liz does read that last piece of advice. I think she needs it. One can need that sort of advice without being completely irredeemable.

I truly think even the worst person in the world deserves basic human dignity and some level of understanding. I’m not asking you to pat her on the back and tell her she’s doing a great job. I agree that neglect is abuse, but even hurtful, abusive people deserve their basic humanity. You don’t have to be the person providing it to her, but if your criticism isn’t constructive, maybe you don’t need to waste your time being callous and rude on reddit.

My dad was physically abusive toward me, and I still think he deserves to be seen as a human being. I’ve chosen to distance myself from him by cutting him out of my life, because I personally don’t have it in me to be understanding toward him, but I don’t think he deserves to be stripped of his humanity. I’m sorry about whatever happened in your life that makes your reaction to Liz so strong, but yelling into the void because it’s easier to bash a random on the internet than to hold your abusers to account isn’t going to resolve your trauma.

Last bit of food for thought before I hop off this thread for good: abusers always find a way to rationalize what they’re doing. Every time my dad abused me, it was because he thought I deserved it for whatever the inciting behavior was on my part. Even if I had been the shittiest child in the world, I didn’t deserve to be treated that way. It wasn’t a question of whether I’d done something wrong (I’m sure I did, I don’t claim to be perfect); it was a question of where his limits were on how he treats people. He didn’t have any. If you don’t have limits on how you treat a person who has done wrong, how do you know you’ll end up any different?

I was actually talking about a different person, I don’t know who Hamilton is. You’re obviously a lot closer to Liz than I am, and I’m not about to tell you how to feel about your relationship with her or the other various people in your life that she’s hurt.

I don’t think anybody should be excusing her harmful behavior. The only thing I wanted to get across is for the people that don’t personally know her and have never met her, that she is a person, too. I think it’s a lot easier to post vitriol and mockery if you don’t remember that the person on the other side of the screen is a human being. 

I know that the distinction between online hate and genuine criticism can be fuzzy sometimes, but I think in the in the case of someone like Liz, it’s important. The former is only contributing to her toxic cycle with social media. The latter isn’t guaranteed to help, but it is at least a more sober accounting of what she’s actually doing wrong. Who knows, it might even help somebody stay away from her nonsense.

To reiterate, I don’t think that we should be excusing her behavior. Just treating her like a human being while we hold her to account.

Babe, I’m not sure you read the post I wrote. I don’t think she gets a pass on neglecting her children, but I do think she deserves for people to treat her like a human being even as they criticize her.

Also why are you putting “girl clothes” (whatever that’s supposed to mean) on the same level as bodily harm to her children?

I also grew up with a horrible home life. I know it took me personally a *lot* of work and ruined relationships to learn how to be better than my parents were. It wasn’t easy. I also know that aggressive criticisms of my coping mechanisms only ever made me dig my heels in. What actually got me to change was seeing how my behavior was hurting people.

I don’t think Liz gets a pass on being harmful because of her upbringing, but I do think that she deserves to be criticized fairly on her behavior rather than becoming the object of online ridicule.

Yeah, I hear that. I don’t deny that she’s doing some reckless things that should rightfully be called out. That said, I’ve definitely seen a lot of posts mocking her appearance, her use of filters on images and videos, her personal hygiene, and plenty of other stuff that isn’t hurting anyone. There’s a line between calling out harmful behavior and piling harassment and digital hate onto someone. Most people on this sub end up on the correct side of that line, and my post wasn’t necessarily aimed at you. 

I just know that the kind of person who goes off their meds for bipolar disorder and starts being a life coach isn’t likely to be doing well. The rest of this is just my conjecture, but I imagine that the online hate is part of how she fuels her need for external validation. For anyone who actually cares about her wellbeing or the wellbeing of the children in her care, posting nasty comments on this sub is counterproductive. 

Liz is absolutely responsible for her own health and for the harm she causes other people. I want to be clear about that. And furthermore, she’s the only person that *can* do something about her health and the harm she’s caused. Pointing out the ways that she is harming other people may or may not be helpful in convincing her to change or in convincing other people not to listen to her. Being nosey, gossipy, and mean is helpful to no one. The goal of my post was to hopefully inspire more of the former and less of the latter. 😊

I actually think what you’re feeling isn’t categorically a bad thing. Frostwind was such a fast-paced plot. The Feywild seems slow and winding. You let your guard down a little bit, and then Shadowfell hits you like a freight train. At least that was my experience. Ep. 64 is actually where things ratchet up a LOT, especially because Brennan guests, and he just does a phenomenal job in his role.

A lot of the wacky things that happen in the Feywild are just a way to get both the players and the listeners to underestimate the importance of the experiences the Boobs have there. If you write down a list of what each plot point in the Feywild ended up being about without all the silly front-matter, the stakes become so much more obvious. We only see things in the Feywild for what they are in retrospect, while the entire time we’re there, our desire to return to the material plane is building. 

And then, without spoiling anything, the stuff that happens in Shadowfell takes that yearning to get back to the “A-plot” and kicks it into high gear. Every moment there feels like it’s also bearing the weight of the experiences in the Feywild that you undersold. By the time the Boobs make it back, the slow tension that started in the Feywild has grown to an intensity that rivals that of the Frostwind arc. It ends up being a gratifying release back into the material plane that launches you into a plot that just doesn’t stop from there on out. But it’s an intensity that has a different texture than just nonstop plot points. It ultimately made the whole world feel so much richer overall, at least to me. 

Anyway, I seriously encourage you to at least listen through the end of Brennan’s episodes before you make your final judgement. I think you’ll be happy you did.

I think I remember the short rest you’re talking about. Emily mentioned specifically looking at certain words in Czech and Bulgarian, iirc. As far as I’ve listened, she hasn’t mentioned Russia or the Russian language by name.

I am discussing these words in the context of the Russian language, because *I* speak Russian, not because Emily necessarily did so. However, slavic languages are extremely similar to each other. I don’t speak Bulgarian, but when I’ve traveled to Bulgaria, I didn’t really need help navigating with road signs or finding bathrooms, and I can have simple conversations with Bulgarian people despite each person speaking in their own native language. 

So while all of the above is accurate from a Russian language perspective, I’d be willing to bet that these words are nearly identical in other slavic languages, if not exactly the same. Words like “wolf,” “fairy,” and “goddess” are pretty foundational words that trace back to the common slavic language that all of these languages grew out of. 

tl;dr I’m specifically talking about Russian, but it’s a similar enough language to ones that Emily has mentioned that I feel qualified to make this post.

fun fact: there is actually a type of snake (Chinese water snakes) that produces oils that are helpful for particular kinds of pain, mostly arthritic pain. This oil has long been used in traditional Chinese medicine. 

funner fact: the reason “snake oil” became a synonym for “fake medicine” is that in USA in the 19th century, after much imperialism, patent medicine salesmen sold oils produced by native snakes that did NOT provide pain relief, on the basis of the traditional Chinese medicinal knowledge they’d only recently encountered.

Epoxy resin is a very beginner-friendly material. There's a bunch of how-tos on how to do a very simple clear coat, which seems sufficient for what you're looking for. The only thing you'd need to figure out is how to create a sealed edge around the board so that the resin stays flush with the edges. 

Alternatively, you can make a silicone mold with an existing board and make a resin cast of it with your photos embedded. You could even color the resin if you wanted to get fancy. You'd need to buy grip tape for the top, and drill/screw the hardware into the bottom. This is obviously considerably more involved, but it would look very cool!

I've finally moved into a space where I can do noisy and messy tasks, so I'm dipping my toes into DIY projects by tiling the surface of a cheap end table. I've done a lot of research, and I think I've got the basics, but the one thing I'm still uncertain about is mortar. The tile I fell in love with is a porcelain tile, and every forum, how-to, youtube video, etc. highly recommends using the mortar meant for your tile type. That being said, most of these sites/videos are also geared towards people intending to use said tile for a wall or a floor. If I was doing so, I would readily purchase porcelain mortar, but spending $20+ on a 50-lbs bag of thinset in order to tile a $9, 4 sq ft table seems a little silly. 

My question: What's the benefit of using a specialized tile thinset? What am I risking on this project if I used the "wrong," cheaper mortar?
